cbv28:0.1: The Discourse giving the Analysis of the Truths
cbv28:2.1: The First Noble Truth and its Analysis
cbv28:4.1: To those beings subject to old age, venerable friends, this longing arises:
cbv28:4.2: “Oh, might we not be subject to old age,
cbv28:4.3: may old age surely not come to us!”
cbv28:4.4: But that cannot be attained merely by longing for it:
cbv28:4.5: this is the suffering from not obtaining what one longs for.
cbv28:5.1: To those beings subject to sickness, venerable friends, this longing arises:
cbv28:5.2: “Oh, might we not be subject to sickness,
cbv28:5.3: may old age surely not come to us!”
cbv28:5.4: But that cannot be attained merely by longing for it:
cbv28:5.5: this is the suffering from not obtaining what one longs for.
cbv28:6.1: To those beings subject to death, venerable friends, this longing arises:
cbv28:6.2: “Oh, might we not be subject to death,
cbv28:6.3: may death surely not come to us!”
cbv28:6.4: But that cannot be attained merely by longing for it:
cbv28:6.5: this is the suffering from not obtaining what one longs for.
cbv28:12.1: The Fourth Noble Truth and its Analysis
cbv28:14.1: He dwells contemplating (the nature of) feelings in feelings,
cbv28:14.2: ardent, clearly knowing, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world.
cbv28:15.1: He dwells contemplating (the nature of) the mind in the mind,
cbv28:15.2: ardent, clearly knowing, and mindful, after removing avarice and sorrow regarding the world.
cbv28:17.1: With the fading away of rapture he dwells equanimous,
cbv28:17.2: mindful, clearly knowing, experiencing happiness through the body,
cbv28:17.3: about which the Noble Ones declare: “He lives pleasantly, mindful, and equanimous,”
cbv28:17.4: (thus) he dwells having attained the third absorption.
cbv28:19.1: The Seven Extra Discourses are Finished
